title: Triggers, data and the evidence that money helps
disclaimer: Listing is not endorsement and is not financial, insurance or investment advice.
review_scope: Source-checked scoping review, not a registered exhaustive systematic review. Regional data availability is distinguished from product use. No premium is derived from macro loss estimates.
schema_notes: All six supplied top-level arrays retained; added infrastructure, loss evidence, research pipeline, monetary ledger, exclusions and source register.
Metric records without a verified financial use have empty used_in arrays; non-payment use and feasibility work are explicit.
Publications reporting studies are not automatically independent evaluations. 'measured' can describe an analysis whose extrapolated result is modelled; kind states this distinction.
Economic_loss is an added monetary kind because economic losses must not be labelled premiums, budgets, limits or payouts.
Empty payout arrays and not verified fields are missing evidence, not zero or never triggered.
Loop/lever mappings are analytical mechanisms; not measured intervention effects.

instruments.name: Parametric heat income cover
instruments.plain_definition: An insurer owes a pre-agreed benefit when a named heat index satisfies the contracted rule, rather than valuing every individual's loss.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Potential income buffer can reduce pressure to work in harmful heat or borrow; causal effect is not established by payout counts.
instruments.risk_holder: Worker retains uncovered loss; insurer holds only the contracted contingent liability.
instruments.who_pays: Members and supporting organisations in the illustrative SEWA cohort; exact premium split not verified.
instruments.who_receives: Covered participants through specified payment arrangements
instruments.speed: Case-specific data and claims process; automatic trigger is not immediate usable cash.
instruments.typical_cost: No transferable price verified; premium depends on trigger, benefit curve, frequency, data and administration.
instruments.strengths: Can pay without individual loss adjustment.
instruments.limits: Needs transparent data/contract and reliable last-mile payment; cannot replace prevention.
instruments.basis_risk: Index/exposure, vulnerability, benefit-size, timing and administrative mismatch.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Targeted informal women workers can be included; membership, documentation, premium support and bank access still matter.

examples.text: SEWA 2024 policy cohort; see separately identified cash layer

instruments.uncertainty: Signed schedule, full timing distribution and causal welfare effects not verified for this review.

instruments.name: Forecast-triggered heat assistance
instruments.plain_definition: Pre-agreed finance and actions activate from a forecast so that assistance can support protective action before the worst impacts.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Potentially protects people earlier and reduces emergency reallocations; actual effect depends on timing, coverage and action.
instruments.risk_holder: Households and public/humanitarian response institutions; no insurer necessarily involved.
instruments.who_receives: Implementers first and selected recipients/services through distinct delivery channels
instruments.speed: Forecast lead is not recipient delay; readiness, authorization and payment clocks are separate.
instruments.typical_cost: Readiness, forecast services, administration and benefit spending; no general heat unit cost verified.
instruments.strengths: Can fund action before observed loss.
instruments.limits: False alarms, misses, targeting errors and payment delays can remain.
instruments.basis_risk: Forecast-impact and targeting mismatch rather than necessarily insurance basis risk.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Targeting can prioritize vulnerable people; this does not demonstrate complete or accessible reach.
instruments.uncertainty: Recipient timing and independent health/income effect need measurement.

trigger.data_source: Satellite data described; exact named product/version not verified
trigger.calculated_by: Underwriter/data process described; named independent calculation agent not verified

premium.paid_by: Member and supporting organisations; exact cohort split not verified.

payouts.recipients: Reported all 50,000 participants; not an independently verified receipt ledger

payouts.use: Flexible assistance; actual per-recipient use not measured
payouts.amount_scope: Per participant, non-insurance cash; not aggregate insurance payout

schemes.name: Dhaka heatwave Early Action Protocol
schemes.insured_or_covered: Selected heat-vulnerable households and exposed groups; warnings, services and cash targets differ.
schemes.heat_basis: Joint temperature/heat-index forecast thresholds activate pre-agreed early action.

trigger.metric: Forecast air temperature and heat index, both in °C-equivalent units as specified
trigger.threshold: Temperature at least 38°C and heat index at least 38 for at least two consecutive days
trigger.data_source: Readiness: ECMWF and/or GFS; activation: BMD and either ECMWF or GFS
trigger.window: Readiness lead 5–7 days; activation lead 2–3 days
trigger.calculated_by: Forecast providers; BDRCS focal point monitors and committee authorizes
trigger.verified_by: BMD/Climate Centre support described; no independent financial verifier named in summary

premium.paid_by: Humanitarian pre-arranged finance; no beneficiary insurance premium

schemes.basis_risk: Inference: forecast or ward selection can miss harm; the joint air-temperature condition can miss harmful humid conditions below it.
schemes.fallback: Readiness and action stages; no universal indemnity or automatic fallback cash for every forecast miss verified.

inclusion.informal_workers: Exposed outdoor workers are a target group
inclusion.women: Prioritization applies; sex-specific cash receipt not verified
inclusion.older_people: Vulnerable older people recognized; complete reach not established
inclusion.disabled_people: Vulnerability and accessibility require recipient-level verification
inclusion.migrants: Registration and temporary-resident access not fully verified

schemes.consumer_protection: Protocol selection/feedback mechanisms apply; independent receipt-time and exclusion audit not verified.

evidence.text: Approved protocol and first activation; not a counterfactual impact evaluation.

schemes.status_note: Five-year protocol approved 2023; first activation 21 April 2024. Current reauthorization/revisions not independently audited.

payment_history.actual_cash_payments: This R6 source set verifies activation; cash recipient receipt dates, paid total and trigger-to-cash delay not verified.
payment_history.speed: 2–3 day forecast lead is not a measured payment delay.

triggers.strengths: Simple, observable and supported by long weather histories.
triggers.weaknesses: Misses humidity, radiation, wind, indoor heat and workload; station/grid may differ from exposure.
triggers.asia_data: IMD daily temperature grids and national station services; local usable hourly coverage must be audited.
triggers.payout_use_status: Verified as one component of a forecast/action financing trigger in Dhaka; no claim that air temperature alone is a sufficient health trigger.

triggers.strengths: Includes temperature and relative humidity; easy to explain.
triggers.weaknesses: Shade-oriented index; not a full outdoor work-exposure measure. Formula/domain and time aggregation must be specified.
triggers.humid_heat: Captures an important humidity effect; not radiation, workload or individual strain.
triggers.asia_data: Can be calculated where concurrent temperature and humidity/dewpoint exist; temperature-only grids are insufficient.
triggers.payout_use_status: Verified in Dhaka forecast/action trigger; not an indemnity or automatically issued household insurance payout.

triggers.strengths: Local natural wet-bulb, globe and dry-bulb sensors integrate humidity, wind and radiation.
triggers.weaknesses: Sensor siting, calibration, maintenance and averaging matter; workload/clothing/individual response remain outside index.
triggers.humid_heat: Captures humid heat and radiant conditions; not a universal personal safety threshold.
triggers.asia_data: Singapore publishes instrument-based WBGT and an API; comparable public coverage across all South/SE Asian locations not verified.
triggers.payout_use_status: No issued heat-finance payout using measured WBGT verified in this review.

non_payout_uses.text: Singapore advisory and occupational action framework

triggers.strengths: Enables spatial/historical estimates without a globe sensor at every location.
triggers.weaknesses: Dependent on meteorological inputs, radiation/wind assumptions and validation; a simple temperature–humidity proxy is not direct measurement.
triggers.humid_heat: Potentially captures humid/radiant heat if full method/inputs support it.
triggers.asia_data: Reanalysis/forecast inputs available regionally; Asian worksite validation of any selected model must be checked.
triggers.payout_use_status: No issued modelled-WBGT heat payout verified.
triggers.background_note: 2008 US-depot model is background. Its validation accuracy is not transferred to Asia.

triggers.units: °C equivalent temperature; dataset often stores K
triggers.strengths: Combines temperature, humidity, wind and radiation in a physiological reference model.
triggers.weaknesses: Reference person/activity/clothing assumptions; grid and outdoor setting do not reproduce every person or indoor workplace.
triggers.humid_heat: Includes humidity but does not remove exposure and vulnerability mismatch.
triggers.asia_data: ERA5-HEAT provides hourly 0.25° gridded estimates across South/SE Asia; modelled exposure, not a dense instrument network.
triggers.payout_use_status: No issued UTCI-triggered heat payout verified.

triggers.strengths: Spatially detailed view of surface heating and urban land-cover patterns.
triggers.weaknesses: Skin temperature differs from shaded air or human heat stress; clouds, overpass time, emissivity and missingness matter.
triggers.humid_heat: Poor direct capture of humidity; LST alone does not measure humid heat.
triggers.asia_data: MODIS daily 1 km day/night products cover region subject to quality/clear-sky availability; HotPay explores LST-enabled indicators.
triggers.payout_use_status: HotPay is concept/feasibility evidence, not a verified live LST insurance payout.

triggers.units: Consecutive days/nights, minima, degree-hours; define separately
triggers.strengths: Captures persistence and reduced recovery opportunities.
triggers.weaknesses: Choice of window and baseline changes eligibility; day/night and time-zone definitions must be fixed.
triggers.humid_heat: Persistence does not itself include humidity unless combined with a humid-heat metric.
triggers.asia_data: Daily/hourly weather histories and ERA5-HEAT night statistics available; local indoor recovery exposure still unknown.
triggers.payout_use_status: Consecutive-day triggers verified; standalone hot-night payout not verified. Do not conflate the two.

triggers.units: Deaths or rates relative to an explicit counterfactual
triggers.strengths: Reveals harm beyond certified heatstroke; supports burden and fiscal-needs estimates.
triggers.weaknesses: Lagged/incomplete registration, baseline and attribution uncertainty; post-event outcome cannot by itself fund pre-impact action.
triggers.humid_heat: Can model humidity jointly, but mortality is not a direct humidity metric.
triggers.asia_data: India facility surveillance and city all-cause studies exist; timely complete national daily death data are not assumed.
triggers.payout_use_status: No heat-specific excess-mortality payout or heat cat-bond trigger verified.
triggers.definition_note: Observed all-cause excess above expected baseline differs from statistically estimated heat-attributable deaths.

triggers.units: Probability of a precisely defined event at a lead time
triggers.strengths: Can release funds before harm; expresses forecast uncertainty.
triggers.weaknesses: Requires local calibration, reliability and decision-cost testing; a probability of above-normal seasonal heat is not a probability of the contracted event.
triggers.humid_heat: Depends on forecast variable; temperature-only probability misses humidity.
triggers.asia_data: ECMWF/GFS inputs used by Dhaka; NOAA GEFS publishes heat-exceedance probabilities. No financial probability threshold inferred.
triggers.payout_use_status: Dhaka uses forecast thresholds, not a verified numerical probability threshold. A probability-based heat payout was not verified here.

non_payout_uses.text: NOAA GEFS heatwave probability products; no automatic financial entitlement implied

evidence_of_effect.intervention: Earlier versus lean-season cash after drought
evidence_of_effect.design: Three-arm cluster RCT; same total assistance, different timing/size schedules; all arms receive cash
evidence_of_effect.sample: 4,144 households sampled across 171 villages; two inaccessible villages excluded from main analysis
evidence_of_effect.outcome: Food security, consumption, well-being, borrowing and livelihoods
evidence_of_effect.result: Larger early transfers improved pre-lean-season food security/consumption and yielded higher combined pre-lean/lean welfare. Traditional timing had advantages during the lean season. No persistent welfare differences after the lean season or nine months later; no discernible livelihood impact.
evidence_of_effect.limits: Drought and agricultural season, not heat; no untreated arm. Earlier-than-lean-season cash was after rainfall failure, not before drought onset. Research partnership is not claimed as an independent external evaluation.
evidence_of_effect.transfer_to_heat: Direct model for testing timing and transfer size, not a heat effect estimate.

evidence_of_effect.intervention: Index-based livestock insurance and drought coping
evidence_of_effect.design: RCT-based insurance study with asset-threshold analysis; reviewed author-institution summary only
evidence_of_effect.sample: Not verified from accessible summary; full paper not inspected
evidence_of_effect.result: Authors report less costly coping, with differences by household wealth.
evidence_of_effect.limits: Full outcome definitions, sample and exact effect estimates not verified here, so numerical effects withheld. Not heat, human-health insurance or a comparison with public cash; basis risk and take-up remain relevant.
evidence_of_effect.transfer_to_heat: Direct model for testing whether liquidity protects food and productive assets; livestock drought thresholds cannot be transplanted.

evidence_of_effect.date: 2024–2025 experience described in May 2026 case study
evidence_of_effect.sample: Interview counts/representativeness not established in accessible case study
evidence_of_effect.outcome: Reported use of cash and implementation experience
evidence_of_effect.result: Reported spending on household and health needs; no counterfactual estimate of health, debt, schooling or work-decision impact.
evidence_of_effect.limits: Illustrative accounts cannot establish causal welfare effects; insurance and non-insurance support must remain separate.
evidence_of_effect.transfer_to_heat: Heat-specific operational evidence, not a completed independent impact estimate.

data_infrastructure.name: National stations and WIGOS quality monitoring
data_infrastructure.owner: National meteorological services; WMO monitoring infrastructure
data_infrastructure.coverage: Country/site-specific; no regional density statistic computed
data_infrastructure.latency: Operational, subject to reporting and transmission
data_infrastructure.verification: WDQMS links data availability, quality and timeliness with OSCAR metadata; this does not certify a financial claim.
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Audit simultaneous usable inputs and missing data within contracted geography, rather than counting all listed stations.
data_infrastructure.caveat: No uniform adequate station density assumed.

data_infrastructure.name: IMD gridded daily maximum temperature
data_infrastructure.latency: Historical archive; not demonstrated as the real-time payout feed
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Useful for historical calibration; not neighbourhood or workplace observation.
data_infrastructure.caveat: Documentation says post-2008 grids use around 180 operationally received stations. This is a product-input count, not the total current Indian network.

data_infrastructure.name: ERA5 / ERA5T
data_infrastructure.owner: ECMWF for Copernicus Climate Change Service
data_infrastructure.resolution: Hourly gridded meteorological reconstruction; product/grid must be named
data_infrastructure.latency: ERA5T about five days; consolidated ERA5 about two–three months
data_infrastructure.verification: Provider quality assurance and later consolidation; revisions possible
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Historical modelling and event verification; waiting for consolidated data conflicts with very early cash.
data_infrastructure.caveat: Reanalysis is observation–model synthesis, not satellite LST or a local station reading. Settlement must define preliminary/final version.

data_infrastructure.name: ERA5-HEAT
data_infrastructure.coverage: Global except Antarctica, includes study region
data_infrastructure.latency: Intermediate daily updates; final monthly updates with two–three month lag
data_infrastructure.verification: Versioned algorithm and source data; intermediate can change at consolidation
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Reference exposure surface; locally validate before contractual use.
data_infrastructure.caveat: Spatially complete grid does not establish complete worksite exposure measurement.

data_infrastructure.name: MODIS MOD11A1 v6.1 and proposed EO trigger services
data_infrastructure.owner: NASA MODIS/LAADS; HotPay prime contractor WEO with ESA feasibility support
data_infrastructure.coverage: Global LST retrieval with clear-sky/quality constraints
data_infrastructure.resolution: MODIS daily 1 km day/night; HotPay also describes Sentinel-3/2 and Landsat inputs
data_infrastructure.latency: Product-specific; distinguish archive, near-real-time and composites
data_infrastructure.verification: Quality flags, observation time and archived product version
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Spatial calibration/context; HotPay explores trigger generation.
data_infrastructure.caveat: Do not substitute LST degrees for air, WBGT or heat-index degrees.

data_infrastructure.name: Singapore WBGT instruments and API
data_infrastructure.owner: Meteorological Service Singapore / NEA; data.gov.sg publication
data_infrastructure.resolution: API reports preceding 15-minute average, updated every 15 minutes
data_infrastructure.latency: Automatic publication; gaps and subsequent corrections possible
data_infrastructure.verification: Instrument siting/calibration and publisher corrections; financial verifier not appointed by API publication
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Transferable monitoring and open-data design; published advisory is not a payout.
data_infrastructure.caveat: October 2026 ministry reply says around 30 stations, expanded from 15 in 2025; count is time-specific.

data_infrastructure.name: Operational forecast and ensemble products
data_infrastructure.owner: BMD, ECMWF, NOAA/GFS/GEFS and other national providers
data_infrastructure.resolution: Run, grid, lead time and event definition must be archived
data_infrastructure.latency: Forecast release schedule; distinguish forecast lead from payment-processing time
data_infrastructure.verification: Hindcasts and local forecast-observation matching; Dhaka monitoring/activation committee described in EAP
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Can support readiness and release before heat; requires operational decision authority.
data_infrastructure.caveat: General product availability is not proof of local reliability at contracted threshold.

data_infrastructure.name: Health-facility surveillance and civil-registration mortality
data_infrastructure.owner: Health ministries, facilities and civil registrars; aggregate analysis by authorized research institutions
data_infrastructure.coverage: India NCDC/IHIP facility reporting; all-cause coverage varies by city/jurisdiction
data_infrastructure.resolution: NCDC expects daily aggregated facility indicators; complete civil-death data can have longer lags
data_infrastructure.latency: Suspected reports early; confirmation and death registration later
data_infrastructure.verification: Clinical review, death audit, registration quality and epidemiological baseline checks
data_infrastructure.finance_relevance: Loss validation, burden estimation and reserve planning; not a verified automatic insurance trigger.
data_infrastructure.caveat: Facility deaths miss deaths outside facilities; all-cause excess is not automatically attributable to heat.

loss_harm_evidence.design: Plant-panel econometric analysis with worker microdata in selected industries
loss_harm_evidence.sample: 58,377 plants in national unbalanced panel; worker subsamples differ
loss_harm_evidence.exposure: Annual temperature distribution / daily maximum-temperature exposure
loss_harm_evidence.baseline: Within-study comparison under alternative temperature exposure, with model controls
loss_harm_evidence.result: About 2% lower annual plant output per 1°C; not a measured 2% fall in every worker's wage.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Registered manufacturing, historical exposure and adaptation; not every sector, informal livelihood or current insurance claim.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Evidence for vulnerability calibration; not proof a particular insurer used this coefficient.

loss_harm_evidence.domain: Work hours and household medical spending
loss_harm_evidence.date: Feasibility report published 2021; precise survey fieldwork date not established
loss_harm_evidence.design: Retrospective survey and comparison group; self-report
loss_harm_evidence.sample: 320 study-group respondents; 80 comparison respondents; income-loss subset 105
loss_harm_evidence.baseline: Respondents' usual work/other seasons, not randomized temperature exposure
loss_harm_evidence.outcome: Reported lost work time and increased healthcare expenses
loss_harm_evidence.result: Study group reported about 2.87 lost work hours per summer day; about 83% reported higher summer healthcare spending.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Local retrospective self-report; unclear field dates; no cash-payment impact evaluation. Nominal expense increment withheld because monetary reference year/FX unresolved.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Can identify timing and spending needs; not a nationally representative wage-loss curve.

loss_harm_evidence.domain: Economic cost of illness-related productivity loss
loss_harm_evidence.design: Two-round household panel, seasonal associations and national extrapolation/valuation
loss_harm_evidence.exposure: Heat-related physical and mental health conditions; seasonal comparison
loss_harm_evidence.baseline: Winter/summer comparisons and counterfactual cost assumptions; not national transaction records
loss_harm_evidence.result: Published economic-loss range recorded in money ledger; disputed workday total excluded.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Survey-derived/modelled national valuation; report and launch release disagree on workdays. Do not equate economic loss with insured loss or sum insured.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Indicative scale for public discussion; resolve methods and denominator before pricing.

loss_harm_evidence.design: City-specific generalized additive Poisson regression, meta-analysis
loss_harm_evidence.exposure: Daily mean temperature above city-specific annual 97th percentile for at least two consecutive days
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Observational city data; not national rural burden. A relative increase on heatwave days is not the proportion of all deaths caused by heat.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Duration and definition affect harm estimates; not a payout threshold or premium tariff.

loss_harm_evidence.date: Reported seasons 2020–21 and 2021–22; published 2025; sowing-year inconsistency in methods
loss_harm_evidence.sample: Four wheat genotypes; 15 replications per condition; five pots used for yield analysis
loss_harm_evidence.exposure: 36/30°C day/night from heading to maturity, with irrigated heat-only treatment; combined drought tested separately
loss_harm_evidence.result: Heat alone: 29.98–46.55% reduction across tested genotypes.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Controlled treatment, not observed national field loss or predicted claim ratio; abstract/methods dates differ. Combined drought-and-heat loss must not be called heat-only loss.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Crop stage, genotype and moisture conditions matter for trigger design.

loss_harm_evidence.design: District panel using livestock survey and climatic variables
loss_harm_evidence.result: Negative heat/humidity-related associations reported for buffalo and crossbred cattle; responses differ by species/season. Exact coefficient not reproduced.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Aggregated observational data and management differences; no national heat-loss total or heat-induced animal death count inferred.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Species-specific vulnerability and productive loss without animal death need separate treatment.

loss_harm_evidence.design: Systematic review and additional back-of-envelope cost analysis
loss_harm_evidence.sample: 127 reviewed papers; cost model combines parameters from multiple studies
loss_harm_evidence.exposure: Climate change/rising temperature; scope broader than a discrete heatwave
loss_harm_evidence.result: Published projections exist, but nominal values withheld because price-base and heat-only attribution were not sufficiently resolved.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Not observed claims, current public spending or an actuarial heat-loss series.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Shows method and evidence gap; do not transfer an aggregate scenario directly into a policy premium.

loss_harm_evidence.sample: One state budget publication; not expenditure microdata
loss_harm_evidence.outcome: Planned heat action activity versus actual fiscal loss
loss_harm_evidence.result: Document plans city heat action plans; no heat-attributable public-spending time series or verified heat expenditure amount admitted.
loss_harm_evidence.limits: Budget announcements/planned activity are not audited expenditure or avoided loss.
loss_harm_evidence.pricing_relevance: Fiscal cost needs event-coded health, income-support and emergency budget data.

research_pipeline.outcomes: Health, labour participation, earnings and exposure
research_pipeline.results: Project page explicitly says results forthcoming.
